text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The United States, expressing concern over decision to make Cambodian Foreign Minister Ung Huot the country's co-premier, has made it clear it will not recognise him in that position because "we see no evidence whatsoever" that First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh's party elected Ung Huot freely to role.
- ASEAN wins the blessings of Cambodian King Norodom Sihanouk for efforts to mediate in current Cambodian crisis. At same time, China pledges it would safeguard authority of Cambodian monarch.
- US Secretary of State Madeleine Albright will visit Singapore July 29-30 to discuss regional developments and review "very strong" bilateral relationship with senior leaders of Republic.
- Information and Arts Ministry bans this month's issue of British Vogue, which it said contained article condoning and promoting drug use.
- Proposed Singapore $60-100 million monorail to link Bugis Junction and Marina Centre may be on track finally.
- Speculators push usually robust Singapore dollar to 30-month low as they drag down Malaysian ringgit and Indonesian rupiah, dealers say.

- Volatility in regional currencies -- with ringgit and rupiah latest targets, after baht and peso -- should sort itself out soon as region's economic fundamentals remain strong, say economists and multinational firms here.

- Thai police raid offices of two foreign securities firms, ABN amro Hoare Govett Asia Investment Research and Capital Nomura Securities, to indentify source of recent rumours government would shut down five ailing commercial banks.
- Singapore music industry appeals to Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong for more government help to stem rampant CD piracy.
- Newly-listed companies in hot demand as investors chase up shares of Chinese drug company Tianjin Zhongxin Pharmaceutical Group Corp and Raffles Medical Group to their record highs.
- Casino operator Genting Highlands says it is slashing room rates by 30 percent after end of promotion to Singaporeans offering 15,000 room nights for as low as S$1 a night.
- Jurong Engineering Ltd sets up joint venture steel fabrication shop in Vietnam, first phase of which was completed earlier this month.

- Mainboard-listed Kuok Group company Pacific Carriers Ltd taked first steps to get into container feeder service and ship agency business by buying 50 percent stake in Malaysia's Triumphline Shipping Sdn Bhd.
- Former Amcol shareholders now holding 453 million shares in Asia Food & Properties can start trading in them today when the Sinar Mas vehicle debuts on local bourse.
